title: Sales Enablement: Complete Sales Kit — Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Deck, Pricing Guidance & Security FAQ
author: Aisha Patel
summary: A single, field-ready sales kit that bundles Redwood Inference positioning and messaging, concise competitive briefs, a recommended pitch deck outline, pricing guidance by product mode, exemplar case study summaries, and a prospect-facing security FAQ.
body:
Overview

This page is the canonical sales kit for outbound and inbound enterprise conversations about Redwood Inference. It harmonizes positioning, competitive talking points, an executable pitch deck outline, pricing guidance by product mode, short case studies you can reference in calls, and a concise security FAQ for prospect evaluation teams. Use the sections below as modular assets (talk tracks, slides, one-pagers).

Owners and SLAs

- Primary owner: Go-to-Market (Aisha Patel)
- Secondary owners: Product (Priya Srinivasan), Security (Liam O'Connor)
- Review cadence: quarterly, or after major product/pricing changes

1) Core positioning and messaging (top-line)

- One‑liner: Redwood Inference — predictable, production-grade LLM inference that optimizes for latency, cost, and reliability across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Primary value props (lead with customer impact):
  - Predictable performance: SLA-backed latency and throughput with transparent per-token economics.
  - Unified API and tooling: Same developer experience across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
  - Cost-aware controls: Batching, caching, and quantization recommendations that materially reduce unit costs.
  - Enterprise readiness: Private deployments, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and fine-grained RBAC.

- Talk tracks by persona:
  - Engineering/ML Engineer: Emphasize runtime optimizations (KV-caching, continuous batching), kernel selection, and per-model perf profiles. Mention SDKs and tracing hooks.
  - Platform/Infra: Focus on Dedicated capacity, autoscaling controls, rollout policies, and cost predictability.
  - Product/PM: Highlight consistent dev experience, quality guardrails, and rollback/canary tooling.
  - Security/Legal: Call out VPC/private options, data residency, KMS/HSM, and compliance evidence.

2) Competitive brief (concise)

Competitors: general cloud AI platforms (CloudX, MegaAI), LLM API providers (APIStartup, QuickModel), and inference infra vendors (SelfServe Runtime, OpenServe). Below is a brief comparison you can use in calls.

Dimension | Redwood Inference | General Cloud AI Platforms | LLM API Providers | Inference Infra Vendors
---|---|---|---|---
Primary focus | Production inference economics & ops | Broad ML services | Model access & simplicity | Self-hosted runtime stack
Deployment modes | Hosted / Dedicated / Private | Hosted-first, some dedicated options | Hosted-only | Self-hosted / open-source tooling
Key strengths | Unified API, cost controls, fallbacks | Integration with cloud ecosystem | Rapid proto / low friction | Deep runtime control but more ops burden
Typical buyer | Engineering-driven product teams & platform | Cloud-native enterprises | Startups & prototypes | Platform teams with infra resources

Competitive rebuttals (short):
- Vs CloudX: "CloudX gives model access but lacks the fine-grained cost controls and unified rollout tools that keep production costs predictable at scale."
- Vs APIStartup: "APIStartup is easy for prototypes; Redwood replaces heavy operational work once you need predictable latency, SLAs, and private deployment options."
- Vs SelfServe Runtime: "SelfServe gives control but requires building observability, rollout automation, and cost-monitoring in-house—Redwood provides those out of the box with enterprise support."

3) Recommended pitch deck (10–12 slides, with speaker notes)

Slide outline (title and 1‑sentence speaker note):
1. Cover — Intro and relevance to prospect
2. Problem — Cost, latency variability, and reliability challenges teams face when deploying LLMs
3. Why now — Model and hardware landscape increases the serving burden (KV cache, batching, quantization)
4. Solution overview — Redwood Inference: unified runtime + orchestration
5. Product modes — Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved), Private (VPC/on‑prem) with bullets on when to use each
6. Performance & economics — Representative benchmarks: latency percentiles, tokens/sec, and per-token cost delta vs typical cloud endpoint (example numbers in appendix)
7. Reliability & rollouts — Canary/A-B, automatic fallback, SLOs/SLA summary
8. Security & compliance — VPC, KMS, audit logs, SOC/ISO references
9. Pricing model — High level (usage-based hosted, reserved capacity, private licensing) and procurement options
10. Case studies — 2 short customer examples with outcomes (latency reduction, cost savings, faster time-to-market)
11. Implementation plan — 30/60/90 day onboarding path, success criteria, owners
12. Appendix/FAQ — Demos, benchmarks, legal contacts

Slide tips:
- Use customer quantitative outcomes (tokens/sec, $/1000 tokens saved) where available.
- Include a short demo or recorded video for 1:1 meetings.

4) Pricing guidance (field playbook)

High-level pricing components:
- Hosted API: usage-based pricing (per-token generation + per-embedding), tiered volume discounts, free trial credits.
- Dedicated (Reserved Capacity): monthly/annual committed GPU pools; pricing split into capacity fee + consumption/overage; discounts for multi-year commitments.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): platform licensing fee + optional support tier and managed services.

Guidelines for packaging and negotiation:
1. Discovery: capture expected QPS, average & peak seq lengths, and percent of streaming vs non-streaming traffic.
2. Recommend mode: Small proof-of-concept -> Hosted. Predictable high throughput -> Dedicated. Regulated data or on-prem requirements -> Private.
3. Anchoring: start with a recommended capacity plan (tokens/month or vGPU count) and map to estimated cost using the pricing calculator (link in related pages).
4. Discounts: allow for 10–25% discount on first-year committed capacity for multi-year deals; larger discounts tied to longer contracts and volume.
5. Procurement: list of required PO/legal terms for each product mode (include standard SOW/MA available from finance).

5) Case studies (one-paragraph callouts)

- FinTech startup (FastLoan) — Problem: high latency during peak quoting traffic impacted conversions. Outcome: Migrated to Redwood Dedicated; reduced p95 latency from 820ms to 210ms and lowered per-100k-token cost by 32% through recommended batching + KV caching.
- Enterprise SaaS (SupportCo) — Problem: inconsistent NLU performance across regions and sensitive PII. Outcome: Private deployment in VPC with KMS and audit logs; consistent latency across regions and successful SOC2 readiness assessment.
- Marketplaces (ListMate) — Problem: spikes in traffic caused degraded reranking quality. Outcome: Canary rollouts and fallback model variants reduced incidents by 78% and improved overall NPS for search quality.

6) Security FAQ for prospects (short, shareable)

Q: How is customer data protected in Hosted mode?
A: Data in transit is encrypted (TLS 1.2+). At rest, logs and artifacts are encrypted with industry-grade KMS. We provide optional contract language for data handling, and dedicated ingestion pipelines for sensitive workloads.

Q: Do you support customer-managed keys?
A: Yes — we support KMS integrations and HSM-based key management for Private deployments and Dedicated customers on request.

Q: Can we deploy in our VPC / on-prem?
A: Yes — Redwood Private supports VPC-hosted control plane and an on-prem package for regulated or air-gapped environments. We provide deployment runbooks and SSO/RBAC integrations.

Q: What compliance evidence do you provide?
A: We maintain SOC/ISO mappings and can provide evidence packages for enterprise evaluation. Specific evidence (e.g., penetration test report redacted) is available under NDA.

Q: How are third-party models and model updates handled?
A: Model onboarding is versioned and supported through our model catalog; rollouts use canary policies with automatic fallback to previous versions on regression signals. We maintain a model change log for transparency.

7) Enablement assets (where to find them)

- One-pager: summary slide for quick prospects (link in related pages).
- Slide deck: canonical pitch deck (editable) and customer-tailored variants.
- Pricing calculator: internal spreadsheet and a public-facing estimator for prospects.
- Benchmarks: perf profiled model list and representative latency/cost tables (see appendix).

8) Field playbook: rapid call checklist

1. Before call: confirm prospect deployment mode preference and compliance needs.
2. Opening 5 minutes: state primary value prop and align on SLOs that matter (p95 latency, availability, cost constraints).
3. Demo/benchmarks: show 99/95/50 latency percentiles and cost delta vs common cloud endpoint.
4. Close: propose next step (POC/technical workshop) and request procurement timeline.
